evidence: Cic. Lael. 24: rēs vēra, opposed to ficta (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: “That’s true” is vērum est or ita est (Traupman 110: rēs ita est); “to tell the truth”, ut vērum dīcam (Traupman 42, 110). With an infinitive, vērum est usually means “it is right, fair” (Caes. BG 4.8, Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: vērum est profectō quod observātō rērum ūsū sapientēs virī dīxēre
phrases.english: it is surely true, what wise men have said from long observation of life

phrases.latin: dēfīnītiō brevis et vēra virtūtis ōrdō est amōris
phrases.english: a short and true definition of virtue: the right ordering of love
